strengths: All the worked numbers match the source: λ examples, the dBm table, FSPL ≈ 80 dB, the link budget (−56 dBm, 34 dB margin), Shannon ≈ 199 Mbit/s, the Doppler shift of 200 Hz, and the quiz answers.

It follows the module's sections in order, and facts left off the slides (the full path-loss exponent table, ITU/FCC/Ofcom, the ISM and 6 GHz bands, the GSM/Bluetooth/LTE dates) are kept in the speaker notes.
The speaker notes are strong. They give click-by-click cues, questions to ask the room, and arithmetic to work aloud, and they do not just repeat the slide.
The animated link-budget chain and the bits-per-symbol chart show the key arithmetic clearly. The frequency-reuse hex grid uses a valid 3-cell pattern.
It meets the requirements: 29 slides, quiz then answers then summary at the end, and the checker passes with 0 issues.
judge.verdict: This is a solid deck that follows the module closely, gets the numbers right and has excellent speaker notes. Fix three things before teaching from it tomorrow: the stray 'Fence:' label on slide 9, the overlapping timeline text on slide 3, and the double markers on the answers slide. There are four animated diagrams (wave, spectrum, link-budget chain, hex grid). The ideas that would gain most from a picture have none: a QAM constellation, multipath or fading, and FDMA/TDMA/OFDMA. The deck also has no Part 1 or Part 3 section dividers to match the three-question structure.

incorrect_claims.claim: Rate grows only logarithmically, so MIMO adds antennas for parallel streams.
incorrect_claims.correction: The source says standards add both spectrum and antennas (MIMO adds parallel streams) because SNR is a weak lever. The slide's 'so' ties MIMO to the SNR column, which makes it sound as if MIMO raises SNR. It doesn't: it adds parallel streams. A slight distortion, not a factual error.
The source says 'microwave ovens'. 'Microwaves' on its own could be read as microwave radiation in general.

strengths: Every number checks out against the source: wavelengths, dBm table, FSPL worked example (−20.0 + 67.6 + 32.44 ≈ 80 dB), link budget (−56 dBm, 34 dB margin), Doppler 200 Hz, Shannon 199 Mbit/s, bits per symbol, history dates, band edges and regulatory figures.

The diagrams are accurate and add real value. The dB ruler is drawn to a consistent linear scale. The ASK/FSK/PSK waveforms actually encode 1 0 1 1 0, with phase flips where the bit changes. The QPSK/16-QAM/64-QAM constellations have the right point counts. The hex frequency-reuse grid has no two adjacent cells with the same letter. The path-loss exponent bars are placed correctly on the axis.
Speaker notes are detailed and timed, give click-by-click cues, add analogies and audience prompts, and link back to the quiz questions without just repeating the slide.
Image placeholders carry specific captions saying what picture should go there.
30 slides, quiz (3 slides) then summary at the end, and the checker passes with 0 issues.
judge.verdict: The deck is accurate, faithful to the source and ready to teach from, with no factual errors and correct, well-built animated diagrams. The only problems are small layout ones: a cramped agenda slide, a narrow bullet column on slide 15, faint antenna-gain steps in the link-budget diagram, and a summary slide that is slightly thinner than the module's own summary.

ui_issues.issue: The 'Isotropic: 0 dBi' label sits on top of the outer circle, and 'equal in all directions' overlaps the bottom of the circle.

The reflected ray bounces off the building back toward the 'Reflected' label rather than reaching Rx. Scattering is only a text label with nothing drawn. The 'absorbed' ray just stops inside the box. The diagram shows the four mechanisms only loosely.

Table headers mix fonts: 'Frequency' is in a sans font and 'Use'/'Wavelength' are in a serif. The same thing happens in every comparison table (slides 7, 8, 11, 16, 23, 27).

strengths: Every number, formula and worked example checks out against the source: λ table, dBm table, FSPL 80 dB, link budget −56 dBm with a 34 dB margin, Shannon 199 Mbit/s, Doppler 200 Hz and the path-loss exponents.
The slides follow all 16 source sections in order, with the quiz (6 questions over 2 slides) and then the summary at the end, as the request asked.
The 'how far / how fast / how many' theme opens the deck, comes back mid-deck and closes it in the summary.

The diagrams that build up on click are well chosen: the wave with a λ bracket, the doubling-distance arcs, the link-budget chain, the AM/FM/PSK waveforms, FDD vs TDD and the hex reuse grid. The reuse lettering never puts the same letter in adjacent cells.

The speaker notes are full scripts. Details moved off the slides (the extra timeline dates, the 2.15 dBi dipole, the ITU/FCC/Ofcom regulators, the ISM band and the 6 GHz band) are kept in the notes, and the notes point ahead to the matching quiz questions.
The checker passes with 0 issues on 30 slides, and the image placeholder on slide 3 has a caption.
judge.verdict: This deck is accurate, complete and faithful to the module, and it is essentially ready to teach from. There are no wrong or invented facts. What needs fixing is small layout polish: the overlapping label on slide 12, the loose reflection and scattering diagram on slide 15, the cramped stats on slide 18, the touching chart labels on slide 21, and the mixed fonts in the table headers. A few source details, such as the regulators and the ISM and 6 GHz bands, appear only in the notes. The summary slide also leaves out the decibel and fading points.
